Day 2 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1259 AM CDT Mon Aug 10 2026

Valid 111200Z - 121200Z

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PARTS OF
THE OHIO VALLEY AND CENTRAL APPALACHIANS...

...SUMMARY...
Severe thunderstorms with damaging wind gusts will be possible on
Tuesday from parts of the Ohio Valley into the central Appalachians
in the afternoon and evening. Isolated severe wind gusts and hail
will also be possible from parts of the central and northern Plains
into the Midwest.

...Ohio Valley/Central Appalachians...
At mid-levels, west-northwesterly flow will remain in place on
Tuesday from the northern Plains to the central Appalachians. At the
surface, a quasi-stationary front is forecast to be located from
northern Illinois east-southeastward into far northern Kentucky. To
the south of the front, surface dewpoints in the lower to mid 70s F
will result in moderate to strong instability by midday. Low-level
convergence along the boundary will likely be the focus for
convective initiation during the day. It appears that an intense
line segment could develop and move east-southeastward along and
near the frontal zone from mid afternoon to mid evening. However,
there is some uncertainty concerning where the boundary from morning
convection will be in the afternoon.

Forecast soundings along and to the south of the front from
east-central Illinois into far northern Kentucky at 21Z have MLCAPE
in the 2000 to 3500 J/kg range. Wind profiles along this
west-northwest to east-southeast corridor have directional shear in
the boundary layer with 40 to 50 knots of west-northwesterly flow in
the mid-levels. Some of this zone could have 0-6 km shear in the 40
to 50 knot range along with 0-3 km storm-relative helicity around
200 m2/s2. This would support supercells with severe wind gusts and
an isolated tornado threat. Some model forecasts, including the HRRR
suggest that an organized cold pool will develop during the late
afternoon. This scenario could result in a swath of wind damage
across parts of the Ohio Valley.

...Central and Northern Plains/Midwest...
At mid-levels, rising heights and west-northwesterly flow will be in
place over the north-central U.S. on Tuesday. At the surface, a cold
front will move southeastward across the northern High Plains, as a
low deepens across South Dakota. Ahead of the front, surface
dewpoints in the 60s and 70s F will contribute to moderate to strong
instability by afternoon. Low-level convergence will aid convective
initiation during the mid to late afternoon, with isolated storms
moving east-southeastward from the northern Plains into the Midwest.

Across the moist airmass, MLCAPE is forecast to peak in the 2000 to
3000 J/kg range with 0-6 km shear in the 35 to 45 knot range. This
will support supercells with isolated severe wind gusts and hail.
However, the rising mid-level heights and lack of large-scale ascent
could result in a more localized severe threat.

..Broyles.. 08/10/2026

Day 3 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0233 PM CDT Sun Aug 09 2026

Valid 111200Z - 121200Z

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS FROM ILLINOIS TO
THE APPALACHIANS...

...SUMMARY...
Thunderstorms with severe wind gusts will be possible on Tuesday
over parts of the Ohio Valley and central Appalachians. Isolated
severe gusts and hail will also be possible from parts of the
central and northern Plains into the Midwest.

...From IL into western VA/NC...
Bouts of strong to severe thunderstorms are expected Tuesday, though
timing and position of the greatest threat corridor is uncertain.
Areas of thunderstorms may be ongoing early on Tuesday across parts
of the OH Valley region, and strong gusts cannot be ruled out at
that time. Daytime heating and a weak surface trough may aid
re-development across the Appalachians and into VA/NC, with
deep-layer mean winds supporting mobile clusters of storms producing
damaging gusts.

Late afternoon and evening development should occur farther west as
west/southwest boundary layer winds maintain a warm and unstable air
mass into IL/IN/OH. The greatest threat of a damaging wind corridor
appears to be in these areas, with MUCAPE over 3000 J/kg, and
potentially 40-50 kt deep-layer shear. Depending on how mesoscale
factors resolve, supercells will be possible, but the primary risk
is expected to be potentially widespread damaging winds.
Predictability is currently low, but categorical risk upgrades
cannot be ruled out in later outlooks.

...Northern Plains...
Storms are expected to develop late in the day over the western
Dakotas near a surface trough over the High Plains. Southeasterly
surface winds and 60s F dewpoints will yield moderate instability, 
and favorable 40-50 kt deep layer shear. The elongated mid to upper
hodographs should aid supercell and hail potential, with bowing
structures producing damaging wind during the evening.

...AZ...
An easterly flow regime will persist on Tuesday, with scattered
afternoon storms over the higher terrain moving generally westward.
Locally damaging gusts may occur with the stronger outflows.

..Jewell.. 08/09/2026

Day 4-8 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
0358 AM CDT Sun Aug 09 2026

Valid 121200Z - 171200Z

...DISCUSSION...
...Wednesday/Day 4 to Friday/Day 6...
From Wednesday to Friday, a broad mid-level cyclonic flow pattern is
forecast to remain in place across the Great Lakes and the
Northeast, as a ridge moves eastward from the northern Rockies into
the upper Mississippi Valley. At the surface, a cold front is
forecast to become quasi-stationary from the central and northern
Plains into the mid Missouri and Ohio Valleys. Low-level convergence
near this front will be a focus for convective development each day.


On Wednesday, model forecasts suggest that scattered thunderstorms
will most likely develop Wednesday afternoon along an axis of
moderate instability from western Nebraska into southwestern South
Dakota. The storms will be supported by a mid-level shortwave trough
moving across the north-central U.S. Moderate deep-layer shear near
the instability axis should support a severe threat during the
afternoon and evening. The models also suggest that a convective
cluster will form within a very moist and unstable airmass in the
central Appalachians Wednesday afternoon, where a wind-damage threat
will be possible.

On Thursday, the most favored corridor for convective development is
forecast from eastern Nebraska into central Illinois. However, the
models suggest that scattered convective coverage could be
concentrated overnight as low-level flow increases across the
region. A severe threat could develop during the day but would
remain relatively isolated due to a lack of storm coverage. An
isolated severe threat could also develop across parts of the
central and northern High Plains during the afternoon. However,
storms there will also likely be isolated due to a shortwave ridge
aloft.

On Friday, thunderstorm swill also be possible from the central
Plains eastward into the Ohio Valley during the afternoon and
evening. However, the most favored locations are likely to be
determined by outflow boundaries associated with the previous day's
convection. For this reason, uncertainty is substantial on Friday.

...Saturday/Day 7 and Sunday/Day 8...
Over the weekend, a mid-level shortwave ridge is forecast to move
across the north-central U.S., as west-northwesterly flow remains in
the Northeast. An axis of instability is forecast from the central
Plains into the Ohio Valley, which will be a focus for thunderstorm
development. It appears that an isolated severe threat could develop
along and near the instability axis each afternoon and evening.
However, uncertainty is considerable concerning the details of any
potential scenario.

..Broyles.. 08/09/2026

Day 1 Convective Outlook  
NWS Storm Prediction Center Norman OK
1225 AM CDT Mon Aug 10 2026

Valid 101200Z - 111200Z

...THERE IS A SLIGHT RISK OF SEVERE THUNDERSTORMS ACROSS PORTION OF
THE MIDWEST INTO PA AND NORTHERN MD/VA...AND ACROSS PARTS OF THE
NORTHERN PLAINS...

...SUMMARY...
Thunderstorms with severe wind gusts will be possible this afternoon
and evening from northern Illinois eastward into Pennsylvania.
Severe gusts and hail will also be possible from parts of the
central and northern Plains into the Midwest, with scattered strong
storms over southern Arizona.

...Synopsis...

A belt of enhanced west/northwesterly flow aloft will overspread the
northern Plains to the Midwest and southern New England
today/tonight. Only modest height falls are forecast at best.
However, several convectively enhanced vorticity maxima are forecast
to migrate through this upper flow regime, focusing several areas of
severe storm potential today into tonight from the northern Plains
to the upper Ohio Valley and parts of the Mid-Atlantic. 

...IL to the Mid-Atlantic...

Early day thunderstorms may move across parts of the Midwest this
morning, but should generally be sub-severe. By midday, convection
could intensify within a couple of corridors. The first being the
upper Ohio Valley/PA/western NY. Thunderstorm clusters will pose a
risk for damaging winds and hail within a moderately unstable
airmass as convection spreads east toward the Mid-Atlantic.

Additional thunderstorm development is expected later in the
afternoon associated with another shortwave impulse spreading east
from IL into IN/OH. This activity will develop within strong
instability and rich boundary layer moisture. Modestly steep
midlevel lapse rates and effective shear greater than 40 kt will
support initial supercells. With time, sufficient clustering is
expected and bowing segments will be possible. Damaging wind and
hail will be the primary hazards, though a tornado or two also could
occur.

...Dakotas into Iowa...

Southeasterly low-level flow will transport mid/upper 60s dewpoints
north and west across SD, with 70s dewpoints common with southeast
extent across NE/IA/southern MN. This will support a corridor of
strong to extreme instability across the region. While coverage
remains uncertain, most guidance develops at least isolated
thunderstorms by evening. Elongated hodographs amid favorable deep
shear will support supercells and bows capable of large hail and
damaging winds. With time, it is possible sufficient clustering
occurs and upscale growth into a bowing MCS is possible as a
low-level jet develops overnight. If this occurs, a swath of
damaging winds is possible across parts of SD into northwest IA,
oriented along the stronger instability gradient. 

...NE/CO/KS...

Scattered thunderstorms are expected to develop near a surface
trough across western NE/northeast CO by late afternoon/early
evening. This activity will spread east/southeast. Steep low-level
lapse rates will support strong outflow gusts and perhaps hail with
this activity.

...AZ...

Mid/upper easterly flow will persist today amid plentiful moisture
and strong heating. This will support thunderstorm development once
again across higher terrain. As storms propagate westward off the
higher terrain, isolated severe gusts will be possible.

..Leitman/Moore.. 08/10/2026
